summary: Trinity County ground lookout site listed as gone. A lookout man was on duty in 1940, and a Forest Service trail leads about 2.5 miles to the old site. No build date found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone. The Forest Service guide calls the end of the trail the site of an old lookout and does not describe what, if anything, remains.

access.note: The Forest Service trail guide lists the Virgin Creek Buttes route among the New River Backcountry trails. The guide does not say whether the route is open or maintained.

visit.trail_note: About 2.5 miles up the ridge from the junction of the Virgin Creek and Slide Creek trails.

events.note: An item dated October 25, 1940, from a Trinity forest report printed in the California Ranger and quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, reports the Virgin Buttes lookout man, who saw five rattlers in his first week on duty.

notes_for_editor: No build date or structure description found. Staffing evidence is a single October 1940 item (dated October 25, 1940). The 'today' description rests on the Forest Service trail guide, which calls the spot a site and does not describe any remains. The spelling differs by source: the FFLA list says 'Virgin Creek Butte', while the Forest Lookouts page and the trail guide say 'Virgin Creek Buttes'; the story keeps each spelling for the source that uses it. Peakbagging.com lists this as Virgin Creek Buttes (LO site), elevation 4760 ft; not cited in the story.
